newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: TENDER SET FOR STATE COMMERCIAL BANK.
newsitem.headline: TENDER SET FOR STATE COMMERCIAL BANK.

text.p: The finance ministry on Wednesday formally launched a tender for 100 percent of the State Commercial Bank of Lithuania, one of the two state-owned banks which is to be privatised.
The ministry in an announcement in newspaper Lietuvos rytas said potential bidders could obtain the tender documents from the ministry from June 5 and bids must be submittted by July 1.

"The bids will be evaluated by the evaluation committee appointed by the ministry of finance. The results of the tender shall be approved by the government of the Republic of Lithuania," the finance ministry said in the tender notice.
A contract for the sale of the shares is planned to be signed 30 days after the deal is approved by the government.

The right-wing government of Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius aims to sell the State Commercial Bank, the third-largest of all banks, and the Agricultural Bank, which is the second-biggest bank in the country.

The governments wants to give a new impulse to the banking sector, which has recovered from a 1995 bank crisis but is still deeply distrusted by the population. The selloff is also part of its agreements with the International Monetary Fund (IMF).
State Commercial Bank was badly hit in the wake of the crisis, suffering a severe liquidity crunch last year.
The share capital of State Commercial Bank is 165 million litas and assets at the end of April were 1.05 billion litas.
Lithuanian private commercial banks Vilniaus and Hermis have already expressed an interest in buying State Commercial Bank. Some Estonian banks have also said they may be interested.
A tender for Agricultural Bank is targetted for the autumn.
